source: native AWS CLI through scripts/aws/aws_cli.py run/result(debug=True)
scope_description: Metric alarm control/admission, retention, filtering, tags; small composite contrast. No metrics published and no action targets configured.
limitations: Single account and region; no alarm action delivery, metric evaluation, or long-term retention tested. CLI-side validation is distinguished from service errors by absent HTTP status.
Valid but absent action target ARN admission not tested: assigned scope prohibited configured actions. Invalid action ARN was submitted with actions disabled and rejected.

No claim about precedence of conflicting AlarmNames versus a nonmatching prefix: tested simultaneous filters matched. Arbitrary DescribeAlarms token acceptance is observed, not a guarantee of every token format.

Three zero-valued period/M/N cases were rejected by AWS CLI parameter validation and are not native service semantics. request_counts counts CLI invocations; native_http_responses excludes these three.
The initial rich update failed because EvaluateLowSampleCountPercentile was supplied with Average. Supplemental valid p90 creation and replacement provide the successful replacement evidence.
Owned alarms all deleted with empty DescribeAlarms results. No metric points published. AWS retains alarm history after deletion; history has no cleanup API used here.

execution_notes.shared_kernel_isolation: One STS call occurred before shared-kernel collision was detected. No controls mutations occurred before rebuilding functions in native_alarm_controls_ns. No peer artifacts touched.

comparison_notes: Captured requests, outputs, error messages, codes, HTTP statuses, request times and cleanup are retained. Only account and generated resource prefix/caller identifiers are normalized; no expected outputs are synthesized.

Scenarios omit redundant writes and reads. The first scenario retains all configuration-changing writes and state transitions for alarm a needed by its captured history. The supplement runs in isolation, so its StateUpdate history comparison selects captured events since supplement creation, rather than replaying earlier generations just for counts.

The driver invokes AWS SDK v2 via replayMetric/awstest.CallSDK on memory and SQLite. A manual clock advances one millisecond per request, never replaying native evaluation latency. Alarm list selection compares exact names/types; configuration/state tests compare control fields, including presence of omitted configuration and raw StateReasonData. Initial service-generated reason prose and SDK-only metadata are not wording oracles.

Native SDK JSON is decoded into the same generated SDK output type as the observed result, preserving optional pointer presence while treating absent/nil response lists as the same empty collection. Tags and dimensions are unordered keyed collections; history order is retained.

Timestamps retain presence, equality and relative ordering per alarm/field across reads, not elapsed native durations. History timestamp comparisons have their own domain because native history creation can lag the alarm configuration timestamp by a millisecond. Retention additionally requires the entire previously observed local history items, including opaque HistoryData and timestamps, remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

History compares event identity/type and parsed old/new manual states (including structured reason data); configuration events compare Create/Update/Delete rather than duplicating every configuration field. This proves no same-state history entries and retained state history without pinning generated summary prose. Initial state reason prose is excluded.

No evaluation timing, composite asynchronous state, action delivery timing, opaque pagination tokens or timed history publication is asserted here. Captured complete history is compared once control writes are locally committed; Main owns timed replay.
